name: Colchicine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 0.6 mg once or twice daily; maximum 1.2 mg/day
1.2 mg at the first sign of a flare, then 0.6 mg one hour later

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or P-gp inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, cyclosporine, protease inhibitors)
key_interactions.effect: Higher colchicine levels; life-threatening and fatal toxicity.
key_interactions.action: Contraindicated in kidney or hepatic impairment. Otherwise reduce the colchicine dose per label Table 1.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Statins (atorvastatin, simvastatin, others), fibrates, gemfibrozil, digoxin
key_interactions.effect: Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, including a fatality.
key_interactions.action: Weigh benefit and risk; monitor for muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially early.

common: Gout flare treatment: diarrhea (23%), pharyngolaryngeal pain (3%)
FMF: abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting (up to 20%)
serious: Blood dyscrasias (myelosuppression, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia)
Fatal drug interactions with P-gp or CYP3A4 inhibitors

contraindications: Kidney or hepatic impairment together with a P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor
monitoring: Signs of toxicity (gastrointestinal upset, muscle weakness); stop promptly if suspected
Kidney function and interacting drugs before each course

pk.half_life: 26.6 to 31.2 hours with repeated dosing (healthy young adults)
pk.half_life_eskd: 18.8 hours vs 4.4 hours in FMF patients with normal kidney function (single 1 mg dose; clearance 75% lower; label)
pk.metabolism: CYP3A4 demethylation to 2- and 3-demethylcolchicine (under 5% of parent); P-gp substrate
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 40% to 65% unchanged in urine (1 mg dose)

sources.citation: Proficient Rx LP. (2022). Colcrys (colchicine) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA022352, set ID d6adc880-5499-4691-93f3-27c87902d5fc, version effective October 1, 2022]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: 'Blood counts in long-term use' and 'kidney function before each course' are our monitoring wording derived from warnings 5.2 and the renal dosing section; the label does not set a schedule.
Two half-life figures exist in the label: 26.6 to 31.2 hours (repeated dosing, healthy) and 4.4 hours (single dose, FMF, normal kidneys). The ESKD comparison uses the single-dose study.
